# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 (Bu-Vb Pc33)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc33
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33
**Title (English, from literature):** Eating meals in succession

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 33 (*Paramparabhojana*, "Eating meals in succession") is a Vinaya training rule stipulating that a monk who consumes a meal before attending an invitational meal commits an expiation offense (*pācittiya*) that must be confessed. In the *Visuddhimagga*, Buddhaghosa notes that strict adherence to ascetic practices (*dhutaṅga*) prevents a monk from contravening the training precepts against substituting one meal invitation for another under Pācittiya 33 and its commentary [Ñāṇamoli 2010].

Text-reuse calculations from DharmaNexus indicate widespread phraseological overlap with other Pali Vinaya texts, particularly Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 32 (§2.4–3.17 ↔ §2.3–4.8 with 0.96 similarity), Pācittiya 57, and the *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text with Tibetan translations of the *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) and the *Prātimokṣasūtra* (D0002), as well as the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* and *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
